interactions.summary: A student names passivity as the result of the sinner's evasions, and Jiang immediately presses the harder question of whether any change is still possible.

Jiang recaps Piccarda/Carter's condition as a vow-breaking spiral: she lacked will, shifted blame, became passive, accepted her lot, and therefore cannot redeem herself from inside the hole she built.
A student proposes that she must regain agency, and Jiang answers that her worldview already defines agency as disobedience to God, so she cannot simply will herself out of it.
A student suggests knowledge, using AI retraining as an analogy for how a worldview might be changed.

claims.claim: Jiang says a vow to God is the most serious commitment a person can make, which is why failing it has the greatest spiritual weight in this example.
Jiang's model of Carter/Piccarda is that vow-breaking, fear, and blame-shifting destroy agency, produce passivity, and leave the person accepting an unhappy fate as though it were proper.
Jiang argues that self-redemption is impossible from within this condition because the sinner has dug a psychological hole and built themselves into it.
Jiang says her worldview is organized around lack of agency, so exercising agency appears to her as defiance of God rather than fidelity to God.
A student proposes knowledge as a possible mechanism for changing worldview, comparing it to feeding new material into AI so its outputs change.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns spiritual damage into a self-built prison: the sinner digs the hole, walls herself in, and therefore cannot become her own rescuer.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we dig a hole and we build ourselves in it
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It compresses the whole problem of self-redemption into one image that makes later grace language necessary rather than decorative.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang compares worldview revision to telling a computer to rewrite its own software from inside its current programming.
signature_moments.source_phrase: It's like telling a computer, change your software.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The analogy explains why agency cannot be recovered by bare command once a person's whole interpretation of God and self is already bent.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's highest-stakes commitment, whose violation deforms the self more deeply than ordinary promise-breaking.
The capacity to act and own one's action; in Carter's damaged worldview it is misread as disobedience rather than fidelity.
The interpretive programming through which a person explains agency, obedience, and guilt; Jiang treats it as resistant to self-editing from within.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture now completes the internal trap sequence: broken vow leads to blame-shifting, blame-shifting to passivity, and passivity to a worldview that blocks self-generated recovery.
